astronomy_picture_of_the_day.title: Eclipse Pair
astronomy_picture_of_the_day.explanation: clipses tend to come in pairs. Twice a year, during an eclipse season that lasts about 34 days, Sun, Moon, and Earth can nearly align. Then the new and full phases of the Moon, separated by just over 14 days, create a solar and a lunar eclipse.
